src/infrastructure/persistence/InMemoryProductRepository.ts: identical doc comment declaring the same snapshot-isolation rule
src/infrastructure/persistence/InMemoryProductRepository.ts: save(product) { this.records.set(product.id, product.toSnapshot()); } has no structuredClone
Both classes copy the same private readonly records = new Map<string, XSnapshot>() storage, with the same findById/findAll restore logic
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
Both files deal with one concern: in-memory, snapshot-based persistence of domain aggregates. Each one implements its domain repository interface through the aggregate's toSnapshot/restore methods. Cohesion is fine.

The problem is a shared rule written out twice. Both classes carry the same doc comment: "Stores snapshots rather than live entities, so changes only become visible once a use case explicitly saves them." Each class then enforces that rule with its own copy of the Map-based store, and the two copies have already drifted. InMemoryOrderRepository.save stores structuredClone(order.toSnapshot()). InMemoryProductRepository.save stores product.toSnapshot() with no defensive copy. If ProductSnapshot holds any nested references, a Product changed after save could also change the stored record. That would break the isolation guarantee the comment promises.

The rule should live in one place, such as a shared generic snapshot store or base repository. Today it is duplicated and enforced inconsistently. Confidence is moderate because ProductSnapshot is not shown: if it holds only primitives, the missing clone has no practical effect, though the duplication and drift remain.

violations.message: This file repeats the snapshot-isolation rule from InMemoryOrderRepository ('changes only become visible once a use case explicitly saves them') but enforces it differently. save() stores product.toSnapshot() without the structuredClone that InMemoryOrderRepository.save uses. The rule should live in one place, not be copied per repository.

This file holds its own copy of the snapshot-store rule and Map-based storage (records Map, restore-on-read, structuredClone on save), duplicated in InMemoryProductRepository. The two copies have already diverged.
